title: Wide-swing cascode mirror
description: The low-voltage cascode mirror. It keeps the matched-vds accuracy of a cascode mirror but recovers the output swing a standard cascode wastes. The trick is the cascode gate bias: instead of the two-diode stack (which parks the mirror node a full vgs above ground), an explicit bias V_bias = vgs_casc + vdsat_mirror places the mirror node at exactly one saturation voltage. The output then only has to clear two stacked saturation voltages, V_out(min) = vdsat_mirror + vdsat_casc, with no threshold overhead, so the output can swing far lower than a standard cascode's vgs + vdsat floor. The two mirror devices still sit at the same low drain voltage, so the systematic error stays near zero. Both mirror devices bind width-first (output width = K times the reference); the cascode is modelled by one representative device (the matched reference and output cascodes share an inversion level). V_bias is author math, and a rule checks it is realizable under the supply.

params.name: V_out
params.note: DC level of the node the mirror serves; the wide-swing floor lets this go low

params.name: gm_id_m
params.note: mirror inversion: lower gm/ID (higher V*) tightens matching but raises the saturation voltage the node sits at

params.name: vds_lo
params.note: the wide-swing mirror node: one saturation voltage above ground, shared by both mirror devices. Retune until wideswing-node-consistent is green (it should equal vdsat_mirror)

doc.title: Reference mirror device (bottom)
doc.description: The bottom reference device at the input current, biased at the wide-swing low node. Its saturation voltage sets where that node should sit, and the output mirror device shares the same vds.

doc.title: Cascode device (representative)
doc.description: One cascode device carrying the reference current; the matched reference-branch and output-branch cascodes share this inversion level. Its vgs sets the cascode gate bias and its saturation voltage sets the second term of the output compliance floor.

params.name: vds_cc
params.note: a representative cascode vds (its vgs and vdsat are the values used, and both are drain-voltage independent here)

rows.name: sys_err
rows.note: lambda mismatch between the two mirror devices; near zero because both sit at the same wide-swing node voltage

rows.name: V_bias
rows.note: wide-swing cascode gate bias: one cascode vgs above the mirror-node saturation voltage, which parks the mirror node at exactly vdsat_mirror

rows.name: sigma_ratio
rows.note: random 1-sigma error of the K:1 ratio; the K-times-larger output device contributes 1/sqrt(K) of the reference spread

rules.note: wide-swing output floor: two stacked saturation voltages, with no threshold overhead (contrast vgs + vdsat for a standard cascode)
the cascode gate bias must be a voltage the supply can produce
the mirror node should sit at exactly one saturation voltage; retune vds_lo to the reported vdsat_mirror if this trips
